note: First Indian Governor-General of free India = C. Rajagopalachari: taught verbatim (NCERT hess208: Rajaji 'served as member of the Interim Government of 1946 and as free India's first Indian Governor-General', claim c67).

Rowlatt Act year 1919: taught (hess208: in 1919 Gandhi called a satyagraha against the just-passed Rowlatt Act, claim c55). Primary chapter HIS-24; in this chapter's scope as a 1919 constitutional-era Act.
Pitt's India Act 1784: taught (IGNOU Unit 23: 'Pitt's India Act was passed in August, 1784', claim c05).

Vernacular Press Act passed under Lord Lytton: taught - the Act (1878, hess208 c43) is placed in Lytton's section (IGNOU Unit 4 §4.4.1 covers Lytton's measures incl. the protests against the VPA and Arms Act, c47; Lytton's ICS age cut c46).

Official key: Warren Hastings 'introduced the system of Civil Services'. Taught with an exam_note: Hastings founded the administrative/judicial machinery (c23-c26) while Cornwallis organised the service (c27, c28); the chapter states both roles explicitly so the key can be matched.

Lord Mayo murdered by a convict in the Andamans: Mayo is taught only for the 1870 financial decentralisation (IGNOU BPSC-102, c52). The murder is in none of the fetched NCERT/IGNOU sources. Source gap - not asserted.

Simon Commission appointed for Indian constitutional reforms: taught in substance (hess208: commission sent in 1927 'to decide India's political future', c56). Primary HIS-25; the Commission's purpose is stated here.

Hindu Widow Remarriage Act year (1856): primary chapter HIS-20. hess205 says only that laws were passed 'to encourage the remarriage of widows' - no year in any fetched source. Source gap - the year is not taught.

ICS introduced during Cornwallis's Governor-Generalship: taught (IGNOU Unit 24: administrative structure from 1793 under Cornwallis; his civil-service reforms, c27, c28; exam_note contrasts the Hastings key of WBCS-2015-Q51).

Viceroy at Quit India (Linlithgow): the Quit India movement is taught (hess208, c70) but no fetched source names the Viceroy of 1942. Section given for context; the specific fact is a source gap - not asserted.

Governor-General at the outbreak of the 1857 revolt = Canning: taught (hess205: 'In 1856, Governor-General Canning decided...' c39; revolt started May 1857, c40; crown_1858 remember-box draws the first-Viceroy inference openly). Primary HIS-19.

Morley-Minto reforms year 1909: taught as the Councils Act of 1909 - first representative element and separate representation (IGNOU BPSC-102, c53; hess208 dates the concession of separate electorates to 1909, c51). Primary HIS-22.

Indian Independence Act 'passed in July 1947': the chapter teaches the Act's outcome - independence at midnight 14-15 August 1947 (leps201, c65) - but no fetched source gives the month of the Act's passage. Source gap on the month - marked untaught rather than asserted.

First Governor-General of independent India (official key: Lord Mountbatten): fetched sources name only the Mountbatten Plan (leps201, c66) and Rajagopalachari as first INDIAN Governor-General (hess208, c67). The chapter's exam_note flags the two question forms and states this gap openly. Not asserted.
Sati banned through legislation in 1829: taught (IGNOU Unit 25: Bentinck legislated against widow burning in December 1829, c34). Primary HIS-20; in this chapter via Bentinck.
Younghusband Mission to Tibet sent by Curzon: Curzon is taught only for the 1905 Partition of Bengal (hess208, c50). The Tibet mission is in none of the fetched sources. Source gap - not asserted.
Simon Commission boycotted because it had no Indian member: taught verbatim (hess208, c56). Primary HIS-25.

Separate electorate provision made in the Minto-Morley reforms: taught (hess208: League's demand 'conceded by the government in 1909', c51; IGNOU BPSC-102 on the 1909 Act's separate representation, c53). Primary HIS-22.

'Black Bill' = Rowlatt Act: the Act itself, its year and its repressive content are taught (c55). Caveat: the nickname 'Black Bill' does not appear in the fetched sources; identification rests on the Act taught. Primary HIS-24.
Rowlatt Act passed in 1919: taught (c55). Primary HIS-24.
Governor-General during Civil Disobedience (Lord Irwin): the CDM belongs to HIS-24 and no fetched source for this chapter names Irwin. Source gap - not asserted.

Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms 'announced in the year' (official key: 1918): the chapter teaches the Government of India Act 1919 and dyarchy in full (IGNOU BPSC-102, c54), but no fetched source dates the Montagu-Chelmsford report/announcement to 1918. Specific-year gap - marked untaught.
Ripon repealed the Vernacular Press Act of 1878: taught verbatim (IGNOU Unit 4: 'He repealed the Vernacular Press Act', c48).

The Act giving enormous powers to repress political activities = Rowlatt Act: taught (hess208: it 'curbed fundamental rights such as the freedom of expression and strengthened police powers', c55). Primary HIS-24.
'Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act' popularly = Rowlatt Act: the Act is taught (c55). Caveat: its official long title does not appear in the fetched sources. Primary HIS-24.
Chamber of Princes (Narendra Mandal) established 1920: not in any fetched NCERT/IGNOU source used for this chapter. Source gap - not asserted.

Charter Act of 1853 envisaged the parliamentary system (via polity pyq_map POL-01/POL-09, which assign this item to HIS-27): taught - separation of legislative function, 12-member Legislative Council working on parliamentary lines (IGNOU Unit 23, c17, c18) with an exam_note naming this PYQ pattern.

First Public Service Commission established by the GOI Act 1919 (via polity pyq_map POL-01, assigned to HIS-27): the 1919 Act is taught, but its Public Service Commission provision is in none of the fetched sources. Source gap - not asserted.
Doctrine of Lapse introduced by Lord Dalhousie: taught verbatim (hess202, c36). Primary HIS-16.
Widow Remarriage Act passed in 1856: same gap as WBCS-2015-Q40 - hess205 mentions widow-remarriage laws without a year; primary chapter HIS-20. Not taught.
First state annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse = Satara: taught (hess202 list begins 'Satara (1848)', c37). Primary HIS-16.
Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857 = Canning: taught (c39, c40; see WBCS-2017-Q105). Primary HIS-19.
